item.name: Introduction

request.description:
## General info

You can use VelHerd API if you have account on VelHerd web site.

VelHerd API is HTTP JSON API. That means all requests and responses are sent via HTTP protocol (secured with SSL). All data in requests and responses present in HTTP Body in [JSON](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON) format.

VelHerd API is based on [REST](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) principles. You have to be authenticated and call the simple HTTPs request on the URLs specified below. The following documentation covers core resources that are used to manipulate the main entities. First of all, read basic instructions to start using the API.

## Very basics of HTTP REST concepts

### Allowed HTTPs request typesemail

- `GET` — Get a resource or list of resources
    
- `POST` — To create or update resource
    
- `PUT` — To create or update resource
    
- `DELETE` — To delete resource
    

### Usual [HTTP response codes](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_HTTP_status_codes)

- `200 OK` — the request was successful.
    
- `201 Created` — the request was successful and a resource was created.
    
- `204 No Content` — the request was successful but there is no representation to return (i.e. the response is empty).
    
- `400 Bad Request` — the request could not be understood or was missing required parameters.
    
- `401 Unauthorized` — authentication failed or user doesn't have permissions for requested operation.
    
- `403 Forbidden` — access denied.
    
- `404 Not Found` — resource was not found.
    
- `422 Unprocessable Entity` - the request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.
    
- `503 Service Unavailable` — service is temporary unavailable (e.g. scheduled Platform Maintenance). Try again later.
    

### Methods

- `Resources collection` => `GET` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/OBJECTS — get list of objects.
    
- `Ids` => `GET` [{{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS)[/OBJECTS/ids](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS/ids) — get list of ids for all objects.
    
- `Single Resource` => `GET` [{{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS)[/OBJECT/ID](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECT/ID) — get one object by ID.
    
- `Create Resource` => `POST` [{{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS)[/OBJECTS](https://operations.cropwise.com/api/v3/OBJECTS) — create new object.
    
- `Update Resource` => `PUT/PATCH` [{{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS)[/OBJECTS/ID](https://operations.cropwise.com/api/v3/OBJECTS/ID) — update object by ID.
    
- `Delete Resource` => `DELETE` [{{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS)[/OBJECTS/ID](https://operations.cropwise.com/api/v3/OBJECTS/ID) — delete object by ID.
    

### Useful tools

- Postman ([https://www.getpostman.com](https://www.getpostman.com/)) — multi-platform REST client for API testing.
    
- Paw ([https://paw.cloud](https://paw.cloud/)) — beautiful (but MacOS only) REST client.
    
- ApiDog ([https://apidog.com](https://apidog.com/)) — a real design-first API development platform.
    

# Important notice! — read before start using API

1. You should add HTTP Header `Content-Type: application/json` for all `POST` and `PUT` requests. Else, request would be dropped.
    
2. VelHerd API works only via HTTPS (SSL). **Important!** — check that you use `https://` in all requests (especially in Authorization request).
    
3. In case of wrong request or data, API gives you response with HTTP Error Code and detailed error description (if available). Please read it carefully.
    
4. Naming convention for OBJECT in requests: you need to use plural object name in `snake_case`:
    

- [{{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS)`/animals`
    
- [{{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}](https://velherd.com/api/v1/OBJECTS)`/company_units`

item.name: Authentication

request.description: The user should obtain a USER_API_TOKEN token that is required for all subsequent requests. USER_API_TOKEN is a string, that should be used to generate a JSON Web Token (JWT). You can generate USER_API_TOKEN on the user settings page (http://{{baseUrl}}/users/ID/edit_user) in the VelHerd system. When you generate a token, you must copy it and save it for future use. After generating USER_API_TOKEN you can use it to generate a JWT.

request.description:
## API Endpoint: Authorization

VelHerd API uses **Bearer Token authorization** based on JSON Web Tokens (JWT).  
  
Before accessing any protected endpoints, the client must authenticate using a personal **USER_API_TOKEN**, which is then exchanged for a JWT token.

### How it works

1. The user obtains a **USER_API_TOKEN** in the VelHerd web interface inside the user profile settings.
    
2. This token is then sent to the authorization endpoint to generate a JWT access token.
    
3. The returned JWT must be included in the `Authorization` HTTP header for all subsequent requests:
    

```
Authorization: Bearer <JWT>

 ```

### Token validity

- Each JWT has an expiration time.
    
- When the token expires, the client must request a new one using the same USER_API_TOKEN.
    
- If a request is made with an invalid or expired token, the server returns `401 Unauthorized`.
    

### Common errors

- `401 Unauthorized` — missing or invalid token
    
- `403 Forbidden` — authenticated, but no access rights to the resource
    

### Summary

- Authentication and authorization are mandatory for accessing secure endpoints.
    
- JWT must be passed with every request.
    
- USER_API_TOKEN should be stored securely and used only to generate JWT, not for direct API access.

## API Endpoint: Farm Units

### Purpose

This endpoint retrieves a list of farm units from the server. It is useful for clients that need to display or process information related to various farm units available in the system.

---

### FarmUnit has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of FarmUnit
    
- `name` — name of FarmUnit
    
- `description` — country_code of AdminRegion
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `active` — does FarmUnit is active and shows in list
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Changes`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    

### Filters by

`id`, `name`, `active`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `name`

---

### Request Format

- **Method**: GET
    
- **URL**: {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/farm_units
    

### Response Structure

The response will contain a JSON object with the following structure:

- **status**: Indicates the success or failure of the request (e.g., "success" or "error").
    
- **data**: An array of farm unit objects, where each object contains:
    
    - **id**: Unique identifier for the farm unit.
        
    - **name**: Name of the farm unit.
        
    - **description**: Description for the farm unit.
        
    - **external_id**: External ID for the farm unit.
        
    - **active**: Active status. Can be `true` or `false`
        
    - **created_at**: Created time
        
    - **updated_at**: Updated time
        

### Example Response

``` json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "id": "1",
            "type": "farm_unit",
            "attributes": {
                "id": 1,
                "name": "Farm Unit A",
                "description": null,
                "external_id": null,
                "active": false,
                "created_at": "2025-06-12T11:43:22.597+03:00",
                "updated_at": "2025-06-12T11:43:22.597+03:00"
            }
        },
        {
            "id": "2",
            "type": "farm_unit",
            "attributes": {
                "id": 2,
                "name": "Farm Unit B",
                "description": "Some Description",
                "external_id": 123,
                "active": true,
                "created_at": "2025-06-12T12:08:15.653+03:00",
                "updated_at": "2025-06-12T14:17:34.497+03:00"
            }
        }
    ]
}

 ```

This response provides a structured overview of the farm units, enabling clients to easily access and utilize the information.

## API Endpoint: Base Units

### Purpose

This endpoint retrieves a list of base units from the server. It is useful for clients that need to display or process information related to various base units available in the system.

---

### BaseUnit has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of BaseUnit
    
- (readonly) `name` — name of BaseUnit
    
- (readonly) `symbol` — symbol of BaseUnit
    
- (readonly) `key` — key of BaseUnit
    
- (readonly) `unit_type` — unit_type of BaseUnit
    
- (readonly) `base_ratio` — base_ratio of BaseUnit
    
- (readonly) `description` — description of BaseUnit
    
- (readonly) `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Changes`
    
- `Single Resource`
    

### Filters by

`id`, `name`, `is_base`, `external_id`

### Order by

---

### Request Format

- **Method**: GET
    
- **URL**: {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/base_units

The response will contain a JSON object with the following structure:

- **status**: Indicates the success or failure of the request (e.g., "success" or "error").
    
- **data**: An array of base unit objects, where each object contains:
    
    - **id**: Unique identifier for the base unit.

    - **is_base**: Is it a base unit. Can be `true` or `false`
        
    - **description**: Description for the base unit.
        
    - **external_id**: External ID for the base unit.
        
    - **created_at**: Created time
        
    - **updated_at**: Updated time

## API Endpoint: Agro Plans

### Purpose

This endpoint manages agro plans — one work type with its resources planned for many crop rotation rows at once. The plan creates and manages its member operations.

- Quantities, areas and spray rates are taken and returned in **base units** (the unit with `is_base` = `true` for its unit type, see `/units`), not in the units the user picked in the web interface.
    
- Nested rows are created, changed and removed through `agro_plan_applications_attributes`: a row without `id` is added, a row with `id` is changed, a row with `id` and `"_destroy": true` is removed. Rows that are not sent stay as they are.
    
- Bulk actions answer `200 OK` with `{"updated_ids": [...], "skipped": {"<agro operation id>": "<its status>"}}` — `skipped` lists the operations the action could not apply to because of their status. `apply_recipe` and `bulk_edit` apply only to operations in `draft` or `planned`. When any operation fails the whole action is rolled back and `422` is returned with `errors` — an object keyed by agro operation ID with the list of messages.
    

### Additional actions

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/agro_plans/ID/add_operations

Creates one member operation for each crop rotation row in `crop_rotation_ids`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/agro_plans/ID/detach_operation

Detaches one operation from the plan whatever its status; the operation itself stays. `agro_operation_id` is an ID from `agro_operation_ids`.

Response: `200 OK` with the plan.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/agro_plans/ID/apply_recipe

Copies the resources of the plan into the given member operations.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/agro_plans/ID/bulk_edit

Changes planned and/or actual values of the given member operations. `planned` takes `planned_start_at`, `planned_finish_at`, `responsible_id`, `planned_spray_rate` and `norms` (`resource_id`, `application_basis`, `norm`); `actual` takes `actual_start_at`, `actual_spray_rate` and `norms` (`resource_id`, `norm`). Norms and spray rates are in base units.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/agro_plans/ID/bulk_status

Moves the given member operations to `status` — `planned`, `in_progress`, `done` or `cancelled` — going through the intermediate statuses where needed. `cancel_reason` is used with `cancelled`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/agro_plans/ID/bulk_detach

Detaches the given member operations from the plan whatever their status; the operations themselves stay.

## API Endpoint: Crop Structure Plans

### Purpose

This endpoint manages crop structure plans — the calculation of which crops to sow on which fields in a season for the best margin, and applying the result to crop rotations.

---

### CropStructurePlan has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of CropStructurePlan
    
- `season_id` — ID of Season (`/seasons`)
    
- `name` — name of CropStructurePlan
    
- `params` — parameters of the calculation (object), see below
    
- (readonly) `applied_result` — what was applied the last time (object)
    
- (readonly) `applied_at` — when the plan was last applied
    
- (readonly) `archived_at` — when the plan was archived
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of CropStructurePlan
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    

### Required on create

`name`, `season_id`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    
- `calculate` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/calculate
    
- `apply_preview` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/apply_preview
    
- `apply` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/apply
    
- `archive` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/archive
    
- `unarchive` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/unarchive
    

### Filters by

`id`, `season_id`, `name`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `name`

### Important

- Quantities, areas and spray rates are taken and returned in **base units** (the unit with `is_base` = `true` for its unit type, see `/units`), not in the units the user picked in the web interface.
    
- `params` keys: `objective` (`max_margin`), `decision_case` (`optimistic`, `realistic`, `pessimistic`), `working_days_coefficient` (0–1, default 0.7), `allow_fallow`, `capacities` (array of `operation_kind` — `sowing` or `harvesting`, `group_key`, `area_per_day`, `source` — `manual` or `telemetry`), `crop_limits` (array of `crop_id`, `min_area`, `max_area`), `crops` (array of `crop_id`, `resource_id`, `min_return_years`, `sowing_window_start`, `sowing_window_end`, `optimal_sowing_end`, `maturation_days`, `harvest_window_days`, `late_sowing_yield_penalty`, `harvest_delay_loss`, `sowing_group_key`, `harvest_group_key`, `contract_quantity`, `contract_price`, `forecasts` — object with `optimistic`, `realistic`, `pessimistic`, each with `yield_per_area`, `price`, `cost_per_area`).
    
- `calculate`, `apply_preview` and `apply` use the stored `params`, or the `params` and `locks` sent in `data`. `locks` is an array of `field_id`, `crop_id`, `resource_id`, `sowing_date` — fields whose crop is fixed by hand.
    

### Additional actions

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/calculate

Calculates the plan without saving anything.

Response: `200 OK` with `{"result": {...}}`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/apply_preview

Shows what `apply` would do without changing anything.

Response: `200 OK` with `{"preview": {"created": 0, "updated": 0, "skipped": 0, "rows": [...]}}`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/apply

Creates and updates crop rotation rows by the calculated plan. Rows that are approved or already sown are left as they are and reported as conflicts.

Response: `200 OK` with `{"report": {"created": 0, "updated": 0, "skipped": 0, "conflicts": [...]}}`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/archive

Archives the plan.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/crop_structure_plans/ID/unarchive

Returns the plan from the archive.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

- **data**: An array of crop structure plan objects, where each object contains:
    
    - **id**: VelHerd ID of CropStructurePlan.
        
    - **season_id**: ID of Season (`/seasons`).
        
    - **name**: Name of CropStructurePlan.

## API Endpoint: Operations

### Purpose

This endpoint manages operations — works done on a field, an animal, a farm unit or a farm unit item, with their resources (applications). An agro operation (`target_type` = `Field`) also carries its agronomic details in `agro_operation`.

---

### Operation has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of Operation
    
- (create only) `target_type` — what the operation is done on
    
- (create only) `target_id` — ID of the record the operation is done on
    
- `name` — name of Operation
    
- `work_type_id` — ID of WorkType (`/work_types`)
    
- `season_id` — ID of Season (`/seasons`)
    
- (create only) `status` — status of Operation
    
- (readonly) `timeliness` — was it done on time, set by the system
    
- `planned_start_at` — planned start
    
- `planned_finish_at` — planned finish
    
- (create only) `actual_start_at` — actual start
    
- (create only) `actual_finish_at` — actual finish
    
- `planned_cost` — planned cost
    
- `actual_cost` — actual cost
    
- `currency` — currency
    
- `work_number` — number of the work
    
- `accounting_code` — accounting code
    
- (readonly) `data_source` — where the data came from
    
- (readonly) `created_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who created the record (the token owner)
    
- (readonly) `confirmed_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who confirmed it
    
- (readonly) `confirmed_at` — when it was confirmed
    
- (readonly) `cancelled_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who cancelled it
    
- (readonly) `cancelled_at` — when it was cancelled
    
- (readonly) `cancel_reason` — reason of the cancellation
    
- (readonly) `reopened_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who reopened it
    
- (readonly) `reopened_at` — when it was reopened
    
- (readonly) `reopen_reason` — reason of the reopening
    
- (readonly) `detailable_type` — type of the details, `AgroOperation` or empty
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of Operation
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    
- `agro_operation` — agronomic details of an agro operation (object), see below
    
- `applications` — array of resources of the operation, see below
    

### Required on create

`currency`, `name`, `planned_finish_at`, `planned_start_at`, `season_id`, `status`, `work_type_id`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    
- `confirm` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/confirm
    
- `start` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/start
    
- `complete` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/complete
    
- `revert` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/revert
    
- `cancel` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/cancel
    

### Filters by

`id`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `work_type_id`, `season_id`, `status`, `timeliness`, `work_number`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `planned_start_at`, `planned_finish_at`

### Important

- Quantities, areas and spray rates are taken and returned in **base units** (the unit with `is_base` = `true` for its unit type, see `/units`), not in the units the user picked in the web interface.
    
- The status cannot be changed through `update`; it moves only by the additional actions below. On create only, `status`, `actual_start_at` and `actual_finish_at` may be sent, so work done earlier can be entered at once as `done`.
    
- `target_type` and `target_id` are set on create only and are ignored on update.
    
- `created_by_id` is set to the token owner automatically.
    
- Details are sent in `agro_operation_attributes`. Nested rows are created, changed and removed through `applications_attributes`: a row without `id` is added, a row with `id` is changed, a row with `id` and `"_destroy": true` is removed. Rows that are not sent stay as they are.
    
- Status flow: `draft` → `confirm` → `planned` → `start` → `in_progress` → `complete` → `done`; `revert` moves `in_progress` or `done` back to `planned`; `cancel` works from any status except `cancelled`.
    

### Additional actions

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/confirm

Moves a `draft` operation to `planned`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/start

Moves a `planned` operation to `in_progress`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/complete

Moves an `in_progress` operation to `done`. `actual_start_at` and `actual_finish_at` are optional.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/revert

Moves an `in_progress` or `done` operation back to `planned`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations/ID/cancel

Cancels the operation. `cancel_reason` is optional.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

---

### Request Format

- **Method**: GET
    
- **URL**: {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/operations
    

### Response Structure

The response will contain a JSON object with the following structure:

- **data**: An array of operation objects, where each object contains:

    - **target_id**: ID of the record the operation is done on.
        
    - **name**: Name of Operation.
        
    - **work_type_id**: ID of WorkType (`/work_types`).

    - **planned_start_at**: Planned start (date and time, ISO 8601).

    - **actual_start_at**: Actual start (date and time, ISO 8601).

    - **planned_cost**: Planned cost (decimal, returned as a string).

        - `planned_quantity`, `actual_quantity`, `planned_area`, `actual_area` — in base units
            
        - `unit_price`, `currency`, `external_id`, `description`
            

- **meta**: Pagination info — `page`, `per_page`, `total_count`, `total_pages`. Pass `page[number]` and `page[size]` (default 100, max 500) to get other pages.

### Important

- `operation_type` on create can be `incoming`, `outgoing`, `adjustment` or `transfer`. A storno is created by sending `storno_of` with the ID of the movement to reverse; then only `name`, `occurred_at`, `reason`, `external_id` and `description` are taken from the request.
    
- One request can write several rows — an outgoing movement is split across batches and a transfer writes both legs — so create answers `201 Created` with an **array** of all written rows, tied together by `operation_id`.
    
- An update changes only `name`, `occurred_at`, `reason`, `locked`, `external_id`, `description` and batch `details`. Movements cannot be deleted: a wrong movement is reversed with a storno.
    
- `details` are batch attributes checked against the resource category. **seed**: `reproduction`, `harvest_year`, `test_date`, `thousand_seed_weight_grams`, `germination` (0–100), `purity` (0–100), `seeds_per_sowing_unit`, `moisture` (0–100), `vigor` (0–100), `is_treated`, `treatment_agent`. **chemical**: `sale_until`. Other categories have no batch details.
    
- `user_id` is set to the token owner automatically.

## API Endpoint: Resource Issue Orders

### Purpose

This endpoint manages resource issue orders — requests to issue resources from a warehouse for operations. Stock leaves the warehouse only when an approved order is issued.

---

### ResourceIssueOrder has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of ResourceIssueOrder
    
- `number` — number of the order
    
- `document_date` — date of the document
    
- (readonly) `warehouse_id` — ID of the warehouse the resources are issued from (`/farm_unit_items`)
    
- (readonly) `status` — status of ResourceIssueOrder
    
- (readonly) `approved_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who approved the record
    
- (readonly) `approved_at` — when the order was approved
    
- (readonly) `issued_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who issued the order
    
- (readonly) `issued_at` — when the order was issued
    
- (readonly) `cancelled_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who cancelled it
    
- (readonly) `cancelled_at` — when the order was cancelled
    
- (readonly) `cancel_reason` — reason of the cancellation
    
- (readonly) `operation_uuid` — UUID of the stock movements written on issue
    
- (readonly) `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of ResourceIssueOrder
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    
- `operation_ids` — IDs of Operations the order is for (`/operations`)
    
- `items` — array of resources of the order, see below
    

### Required on create

`document_date`, `operation_ids`, `items`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `approve` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/resource_issue_orders/ID/approve
    
- `issue` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/resource_issue_orders/ID/issue
    
- `cancel` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/resource_issue_orders/ID/cancel
    

### Filters by

`id`, `number`, `status`, `warehouse_id`, `document_date`, `operation_uuid`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `document_date`

### Important

- Create takes `document_date`, `number` (optional), `description` (optional), `operation_ids` and `items` — an array of `resource_id`, `planned_quantity`, `warehouse_id`. Items are split by warehouse, so one request can create **several** orders: create answers `201 Created` with an array of all created orders and `meta.duplicates` — open orders that may already cover the same operations.
    
- Update is possible only for an `approved` order and changes only issued quantities: `items_attributes` — array of `id`, `issued_quantity`.
    
- The status cannot be changed through `update`; it moves only by the additional actions below. Status flow: `planned` → `approve` → `approved` → `issue` → `issued`; `cancel` works from `planned` and `approved`. Orders cannot be deleted.
    

### Additional actions

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/resource_issue_orders/ID/approve

Approves a `planned` order.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/resource_issue_orders/ID/issue

Issues an `approved` order: writes the outgoing stock movements. `items` sets the issued quantity of each item; `issued_on` (date) is optional and defaults to now.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/resource_issue_orders/ID/cancel

Cancels a `planned` or `approved` order. **Note:** `reason` is required and is sent at the top level of the body, not inside `data`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

## API Endpoint: Land Documents

### Purpose

This endpoint manages land documents — lease, sublease, emphyteusis, purchase and other agreements on land parcels, with their payment terms and scans.

---

### LandDocument has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of LandDocument

- `payment_form` — form of the payment
    
- `payment_rate_type` — how the payment is calculated
    
- `payment_amount` — payment amount
    
- `payment_percent` — payment as percent of the valuation
    
- `currency` — currency
    
- `payment_frequency` — frequency of the payment
    
- `payment_resource_id` — ID of Resource paid in kind (`/resources`)
    
- `payment_quantity` — quantity of the resource paid in kind
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of LandDocument
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    
- `land_document_parcels` — array of parcels of the document with their parties, see below
    
- (readonly) `files` — array of attached scans: `id`, `filename`, `content_type`, `byte_size`
    
- (write-only) `file_signed_ids` — array of `signed_id` from **Direct Uploads** to attach
    
- (write-only) `removed_file_ids` — array of IDs of attached files to remove
    

### Required on create

`document_type`, `start_date`, `status`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    

### Filters by

`id`, `document_type`, `number`, `status`, `registration_number`, `payment_resource_id`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `signed_on`, `start_date`

### Important

- Parcels are sent in `land_document_parcels_attributes`, parties of each parcel in its `land_document_parties_attributes`. Nested rows are created, changed and removed through `land_document_parcels_attributes`: a row without `id` is added, a row with `id` is changed, a row with `id` and `"_destroy": true` is removed. Rows that are not sent stay as they are.

`id`, `name`, `work_type_id`, `machine_type_id`, `active`, `external_id`

### Important

- `output_rate` and `fuel_rate` are taken and returned in the **planning unit of the work type's rate basis** exactly as stored (hectares, tonnes, kilometres…): `output_rate` is units per shift, `fuel_rate` is litres per unit. They are not converted to the units the user picked in the web interface.

## API Endpoint: Machine Tasks

### Purpose

This endpoint manages machine tasks — works assigned to one machine with its implements on the fields of a basis: an agro plan or a list of agro operations. A task is an Operation with the `MachineTask` detail, so it shares the statuses, events and rights of `/operations`, but the plain operations endpoint neither lists nor changes tasks, and this one never touches a field or animal work.

---

### MachineTask has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of the Operation the task is
    
- `name` — name of MachineTask; filled in from the work type when empty
    
- `work_type_id` — ID of WorkType of the `agro` category, the same as the basis has (`/work_types`)
    
- `season_id` — ID of Season, the same as the basis has (`/seasons`)
    
- (create only) `status` — status of MachineTask
    
- (readonly) `timeliness` — was it done on time, set by the system
    
- `planned_start_at` — planned start
    
- `planned_finish_at` — planned finish
    
- (readonly) `actual_start_at` — actual start, set by the events
    
- (readonly) `actual_finish_at` — actual finish, set by the events
    
- `planned_cost` — planned cost
    
- `actual_cost` — actual cost
    
- `currency` — currency
    
- `work_number` — number of the work
    
- `accounting_code` — accounting code
    
- (readonly) `data_source` — where the data came from
    
- (readonly) `created_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who created the record (the token owner)
    
- (readonly) `confirmed_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who confirmed it
    
- (readonly) `confirmed_at` — when it was confirmed
    
- (readonly) `cancelled_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who cancelled it
    
- (readonly) `cancelled_at` — when it was cancelled
    
- (readonly) `cancel_reason` — reason of the cancellation
    
- (readonly) `reopened_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who reopened it
    
- (readonly) `reopened_at` — when it was reopened
    
- (readonly) `reopen_reason` — reason of the reopening
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of MachineTask
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    
- `machine_task` — the machine, the implements and the basis of the task (object), see below
    

### Required on create

`machine_task_attributes.machine_id`, `planned_finish_at`, `planned_start_at`, `season_id`, `work_type_id`, and one basis: `machine_task_attributes.agro_plan_id` or `machine_task_attributes.agro_operation_ids`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    
- `confirm` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/confirm
    
- `start` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/start
    
- `complete` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/complete
    
- `revert` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/revert
    
- `cancel` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/cancel
    
- `reopen` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/reopen
    

### Filters by

`id`, `work_type_id`, `season_id`, `status`, `timeliness`, `work_number`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `planned_start_at`, `planned_finish_at`

### Important

- `id` is the ID of the operation, the same as in `/operations`; the ID of the detail is `machine_task.id`, and that is what `machine_task_id` of `/machine_task_shifts` refers to.
    
- The status cannot be changed through `update`; it moves only by the additional actions below. On create only, `status` may be `draft` or `planned`.
    
- The detail is sent in `machine_task_attributes`: `machine_id`, `equipment_ids` (array, the full list — what is left out is unhitched), `machinery_aggregate_id`, and exactly one basis: `agro_plan_id` or `agro_operation_ids` (array of `agro_operation.id` from `/operations`). The basis must be of the same work type and season as the task.
    
- A task cannot carry a target or applications of its own: materials are applied in the agro operations of the basis.
    
- With an aggregate, the machine must be of its machine class and the implements of its implement classes; written-off units and stationary equipment are refused.
    
- `created_by_id` is set to the token owner automatically.
    
- Status flow: `draft` → `confirm` → `planned` → `start` → `in_progress` → `complete` → `done`; `revert` moves `in_progress` or `done` back to `planned`; `reopen` moves `done` back to `in_progress`; `cancel` works from any status except `cancelled`.
    

### Additional actions

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/confirm

Moves a `draft` task to `planned`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/start

Moves a `planned` task to `in_progress`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/complete

Moves an `in_progress` task to `done`. `actual_start_at` and `actual_finish_at` are optional.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/revert

Moves an `in_progress` or `done` task back to `planned`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/cancel

Cancels the task. `cancel_reason` is optional.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks/ID/reopen

Moves a `done` task back to `in_progress` so more shifts can be recorded; `reopen_reason` is required and `reopened_by_id` is set to the token owner. Reopening is a right of its own: a `user` role gets it only through the `reopen` permission on operations.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

---

### Request Format

- **Method**: GET
    
- **URL**: {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machine_tasks
    

### Response Structure

The response will contain a JSON object with the following structure:

- **data**: An array of machine task objects, where each object contains:
    
    - **id**: VelHerd ID of the Operation the task is.
        
    - **name**: Name of MachineTask; filled in from the work type when empty.
        
    - **work_type_id**: ID of WorkType of the `agro` category, the same as the basis has (`/work_types`).
        
    - **season_id**: ID of Season, the same as the basis has (`/seasons`).
        
    - **status**: Status of MachineTask. Can be one of `draft`, `planned`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled`.
        
    - **timeliness**: Was it done on time, set by the system. Can be one of `early`, `on_time`, `late`.
        
    - **planned_start_at**: Planned start (date and time, ISO 8601).
        
    - **planned_finish_at**: Planned finish (date and time, ISO 8601).
        
    - **actual_start_at**: Actual start, set by the events (date and time, ISO 8601).
        
    - **actual_finish_at**: Actual finish, set by the events (date and time, ISO 8601).
        
    - **planned_cost**: Planned cost.
        
    - **actual_cost**: Actual cost.
        
    - **currency**: Currency. Can be one of `usd`, `eur`, `uah`, `gbp`.
        
    - **work_number**: Number of the work.
        
    - **accounting_code**: Accounting code.
        
    - **data_source**: Where the data came from.
        
    - **created_by_id**: ID of the VelHerd user who created the record (the token owner).
        
    - **confirmed_by_id**: ID of the VelHerd user who confirmed it.
        
    - **confirmed_at**: When it was confirmed (date and time, ISO 8601).
        
    - **cancelled_by_id**: ID of the VelHerd user who cancelled it.
        
    - **cancelled_at**: When it was cancelled (date and time, ISO 8601).
        
    - **cancel_reason**: Reason of the cancellation.
        
    - **reopened_by_id**: ID of the VelHerd user who reopened it.
        
    - **reopened_at**: When it was reopened (date and time, ISO 8601).
        
    - **reopen_reason**: Reason of the reopening.
        
    - **external_id**: An optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system.
        
    - **description**: Description of MachineTask.
        
    - **created_at**: Created time
        
    - **updated_at**: Updated time
        
    - **machine_task**: The machine, the implements and the basis of the task (object), see below.
        
        - `id` — the ID a shift refers to as `machine_task_id`
            
        - `machine_id` — the machine (`/machines`)
            
        - `machinery_aggregate_id` — the aggregate whose norms the task is counted by (`/machinery_aggregates`)
            
        - `agro_plan_id` — the plan the task serves (`/agro_plans`), or empty
            
        - `equipment_ids` — array of hitched implements (`/equipments`)
            
        - `agro_operation_ids` — array of agro operations of the basis when the task serves a list, empty with a plan
            
        - `external_id`, `description`
            

- **meta**: Pagination info — `page`, `per_page`, `total_count`, `total_pages`. Pass `page[number]` and `page[size]` (default 100, max 500) to get other pages.

## API Endpoint: Machine Task Shifts

### Purpose

This endpoint manages the shifts of machine tasks — a driver's spell on the machine with what it did on each agro operation of the basis. The works of a shift are the facts: the agro operation takes the sum of them as its actual area and actual quantities, recounted by the system on every save and delete.

---

### MachineTaskShift has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of MachineTaskShift
    
- (create only) `machine_task_id` — ID of the task detail — `machine_task.id` from `/machine_tasks`, not the operation ID
    
- `driver_id` — ID of Employee who drove (`/employees`)
    
- `started_at` — start of the shift
    
- `finished_at` — end of the shift, not later than now
    
- `engine_hours_start` — engine hours counter at the start
    
- `engine_hours_end` — engine hours counter at the end, not lower than at the start
    
- `fuel_quantity` — fuel used, in the base volume unit
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of MachineTaskShift
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    
- `shift_works` — array of what the shift did on each agro operation, see below
    

### Required on create

`finished_at`, `machine_task_id`, `started_at`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    

### Filters by

`id`, `machine_task_id`, `driver_id`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `started_at`

### Important

- `worked_area`, `fuel_quantity` and the applied `quantity` are taken and returned in **base units** (the unit with `is_base` = `true` for its unit type, see `/units`), not in the units the user picked in the web interface.
    
- Reading needs the right to see operations; creating, changing and deleting a shift need the right to update operations — a shift is part of its task, so a manager may delete one though a manager may not delete a work.
    
- A shift is recorded only on a `planned` or `in_progress` task, and only on agro operations of the task's basis that are `planned` or `in_progress`; a closed agro operation keeps its facts until reopened.
    
- `machine_task_id` is set on create only and is ignored on update.
    
- Works are sent in `shift_works_attributes`, the resources a work applied in `shift_work_applications_attributes` inside it: a row without `id` is added, a row with `id` is changed, a row with `id` and `"_destroy": true` is removed. Rows that are not sent stay as they are. A resource may be reported only on a work type that takes applications.
    
- A delete the task or an agro operation refuses answers `422` with `errors` instead of `204`.
    

---

## API Endpoint: Tech Maps

### Purpose

This endpoint manages tech maps — how a crop is grown: the ordered works with their machinery norms and recipes, independent of the season. The rows live in `/tech_map_rows`. A map without a crop is a library map: a source of rows for other maps, never deployed itself.

---

### TechMap has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of TechMap
    
- `name` — name of TechMap, unique for the crop and the predecessor
    
- `crop_id` — ID of Crop the map grows (`/crops`); empty for a library map
    
- `predecessor_crop_id` — ID of Crop the map follows (`/crops`), not the crop itself
    
- (readonly) `status` — status of TechMap
    
- (readonly) `approved_by_id` — ID of the VelHerd user who approved it
    
- (readonly) `approved_at` — when it was approved
    
- `planned_area` — default crop area the map is read for, base area unit
    
- `fuel_resource_id` — ID of Resource of the `fuel` category the map is priced by (`/resources`)
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of TechMap
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    

### Required on create

`name`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    
- `approve` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_maps/ID/approve
    
- `archive` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_maps/ID/archive
    
- `compose` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_maps/ID/compose
    

### Filters by

`id`, `name`, `crop_id`, `predecessor_crop_id`, `status`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `name`

### Important

- `planned_area` are taken and returned in **base units** (the unit with `is_base` = `true` for its unit type, see `/units`), not in the units the user picked in the web interface.

### Additional actions

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_maps/ID/approve

## API Endpoint: Tech Map Rows

### Purpose

This endpoint manages the rows of tech maps — one work of a map: a snapshot of a template's recipe and of an aggregate's norms, plus what only the map knows: the share of the crop area and the timing relative to the base work. Copies, not references: editing the handbook never rewrites a map somebody has already costed.

---

### TechMapRow has next parameters

- (readonly) `id` — VelHerd ID of TechMapRow
    
- (create only) `tech_map_id` — ID of TechMap (`/tech_maps`)
    
- (readonly) `position` — order of the row in the map; a new row is appended, `move` changes it
    
- `name` — name of TechMapRow
    
- `work_type_id` — ID of WorkType of the `agro` category (`/work_types`)
    
- (readonly) `source_template_id` — ID of AgroOperationTemplate the recipe was taken from (`/agro_operation_templates`)
    
- (readonly) `source_tech_map_id` — ID of TechMap the row was composed from (`/tech_maps`)
    
- `machinery_aggregate_id` — ID of MachineryAggregate of the same work type (`/machinery_aggregates`); sent alone, it fills the norms below
    
- `output_rate` — output norm, units of the rate basis per shift
    
- `fuel_rate` — fuel norm, litres per unit of the rate basis
    
- `shift_hours` — hours in a shift
    
- `operators_count` — operators per shift
    
- `auxiliary_workers_count` — auxiliary workers per shift
    
- `area_share` — share of the crop area the work covers, percent, `100` by default
    
- `base` — is this the base work (sowing) the timing of the others counts from; one per map
    
- `day_offset` — days from the base work, negative before it; dropped for the base row
    
- `duration_days` — how many days the work takes, `10` by default
    
- `planned_spray_rate` — spray rate of the recipe, base volume unit; required with tank-mix positions
    
- `external_id` — an optional identifier used to reference this resource in an external system
    
- `description` — description of TechMapRow
    
- (readonly) `created_at`
    
- (readonly) `updated_at`
    
- `tech_map_row_applications` — array of recipe positions, see below
    

### Required on create

`name`, `tech_map_id`, `work_type_id`

### Acceptable methods

- `Ids`
    
- `Single Resource`
    
- `Create Resource`
    
- `Update Resource`
    
- `Delete Resource`
    
- `refresh` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_map_rows/ID/refresh
    
- `move` — `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_map_rows/ID/move
    

### Filters by

`id`, `tech_map_id`, `work_type_id`, `machinery_aggregate_id`, `source_template_id`, `base`, `external_id`

### Order by

`id`, `position`

### Important

- `output_rate` and `fuel_rate` are taken and returned in the **planning unit of the work type's rate basis** exactly as stored (hectares, tonnes, kilometres…): `output_rate` is units per shift, `fuel_rate` is litres per unit. They are not converted to the units the user picked in the web interface. `planned_spray_rate` and `planned_quantity` are taken and returned in **base units** (the unit with `is_base` = `true` for its unit type, see `/units`), not in the units the user picked in the web interface.
    
- A row may be snapshotted from a template: send `template_id` with `tech_map_id` on create, and the template's name, work type, spray rate and recipe come first, the other attributes sent go on top. Later edits of the template do not touch the row; `refresh` re-takes the snapshot.
    
- Recipe positions are sent in `tech_map_row_applications_attributes`: a row without `id` is added, a row with `id` is changed, a row with `id` and `"_destroy": true` is removed. Rows that are not sent stay as they are. Positions are numbered in the order they are sent; `application_basis` is `per_area` or `per_solution`, and `per_solution` needs `in_tank_mix`. A recipe needs a work type that takes applications.
    
- `tech_map_id` is set on create only and is ignored on update; `position` is the map's own and moves only by `move`. Deleting a row renumbers the rest.
    

### Additional actions

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_map_rows/ID/refresh

Re-takes the snapshot from the sources: the recipe and the spray rate from `source_template_id`, the norms from `machinery_aggregate_id`. The name, the area share and the timing are left alone. A row without a source returns `422`.

Response: `200 OK` with the updated record in the same format as **Single Resource**. An action that is not allowed from the current status returns `422` with `errors`.

#### `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/tech_map_rows/ID/move

Swaps places with the neighbour above (`direction` = `up`) or below (`down`); a row already at the edge stays put.

Response: `200 OK` with the row in the same format as **Single Resource**.

---

## API Endpoint: Machinery Schedule

### Purpose

This endpoint reads the machinery schedule of a season — how many machines and implements of each class the season's agro plans need day by day, against the units the fleet has. The schedule is computed from the plans, the tech maps and the fleet, never stored, so it is read only and has no records of its own: there is no `ids`, no single resource, no pagination.

---

### Request Format

- **Method**: GET

- **URL**: {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/machinery_schedule?season_id=ID


`season_id` is required: without it the response is `422`, for an unknown season `404`.

### Acceptable methods

- `Resources collection` only


### Important

- Areas are returned in the **base area unit** (see `/units`), not in the unit the user picked in the web interface.

- A plan's shifts are spread evenly over the calendar days of its window; an aggregate is split into its classes, so two aggregates pulled by the same tractor class compete for it. The need of a class on a day is rounded up only after the works of the day are summed.

- A unit under repair still counts as available; only a written-off unit has left the yard.

- A plan the schedule cannot count stays in `works` with its `reason` instead of its shifts: `no_aggregate`, `no_area`, `basis_not_supported` (the work type is not counted per area), `norm_not_set`.

- Reading needs the `MachinerySchedule` permission (read), which a company role may grant without granting the fleet or the plans.


### Response Structure

The response will contain a JSON object with the following structure:

- **season**: `id` and `name` of the season.

- **areaUnitLabel**: Symbol of the base area unit the areas are in.

- **decades**: The axis — every calendar decade (the 1st–10th, the 11th–20th and the 21st to the month's end) from the first busy day to the last, the empty ones included: `key` (ISO date of the first day), `number` (1–3), `startOn`, `endOn`.

- **lines**: One row per class of machines and implements the plans need, machines first: `key`, `kind` (`machine_type` or `equipment_type`), `name`, `available` (units in service), `peak` (most units needed on one day of the season), `deficit` (is any day short), `contractArea` (area no own unit can take over the season), `decades` — per decade `key`: `needed` (busiest day of the decade), `deficit` (units short on that day), `contractArea`.

- **bottlenecks**: The decades a class is short in: `key`, `className`, `available`, `needed`, `deficit`, `contractArea`, `startOn`, `endOn`.

- **works**: The plans the schedule is built from: `key`, `name`, `source` (`plan`, or `forecast` for a plan still expected from an approved tech map), `planId`, `reason` (why it is not counted, or empty), `techMapId`, `techMapName`, `farmUnitItemName`, `workTypeName`, `aggregateName`, `startOn`, `finishOn`, `area`, `shifts`.

- **summary**: `worksCount`, `forecastCount`, `gapsCount` (works with a `reason`), `deficitClassesCount`.

## API Endpoint: Direct Uploads

### Purpose

The first step of attaching a file through the API (land document scans, employee document scans). The file itself is not sent here: the endpoint returns a URL to upload the file to storage directly, and a `signed_id` to pass to the record afterwards.

---

### How to attach a file

1. `POST` {{baseUrl}}/api/{{apiVersion}}/direct_uploads with `blob`: `filename`, `byte_size` (bytes), `checksum` (Base64-encoded MD5 of the file), `content_type`.
    
2. `PUT` the file bytes to `direct_upload.url` with exactly the headers from `direct_upload.headers`. No `Authorization` header is needed for this request.
    
3. Pass `signed_id` in `file_signed_ids` when creating or updating the record.
    

### Important

- Accounts with read-only access (`manager_read`, `guest`, `no_access`) get `403`.
    
- A `signed_id` works only within the company of the token.
    

### Example Response

``` json
{
    "signed_id": "eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NDIsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--1a2b3c",
    "filename": "lease-scan.pdf",
    "byte_size": 482113,
    "content_type": "application/pdf",
    "direct_upload": {
        "url": "https://storage.example.com/uploads/abc123?signature=...",
        "headers": {
            "Content-Type": "application/pdf",
            "Content-MD5": "kH4yK0hYd8Qh0m5XoE0e4w=="
        }
    }
}

 ```
